summary: One blocking finding, STU-011, and it is repaired. The first reading attached (Ps~53:1) to the third of the four scriptural texts Chrysostom sets beside "thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself" in In Mt. hom. 71 -- "The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God ... They are corrupt, and become abominable in their ways" -- and those words are not Ps 53's in either numbering. Verified in the library's own tracked editions rather than from the finding: the Clementine Vulgate gives Ps 13:1 as Dixit insipiens in corde suo: Non est Deus. Corrupti sunt, et abominabiles facti sunt in studiis suis, and the Douay-Rheims (Challoner) renders that verse in the very words the study quotes; Ps 52:1-2, which the Hebrew numbers 53, has instead abominabiles facti sunt in iniquitatibus; and Ps 53 in the Missal's own Vulgate numbering is Deus, in nomine tuo salvum me fac, which has nothing to do with the sentence. sections/20-whole-heart-one-body.tex now cites Ps~13:1; Heb.\ 14:1, the Missal's numbering with the Hebrew beside it, as sections/05-appointed-texts.tex says the study cites psalms and as the 1962 profile requires. A sweep of every psalm number printed in the nine components of main.tex finds Pss 32, 75, 101, 109 and 118 and no other, all in the Missal's numbering, so no bare Hebrew-numbered psalm citation remains in the study. One premise of the finding is wrong and is reported here rather than silently worked around. STU-011 states that the New Advent text of Homily 71 prints the quotation "without a verse reference of its own, so the locus is the study's, not the translator's". The tracked CCEL transcription of NPNF1 10 -- the same artifact the source binding passage.john-chrysostom.homiliae-in-matthaeum.ccel-web-2026-09-17.homily-71 records, read at physical lines 39940-40343 of artifact ccel-text-adb8f1c9 -- carries a numbered note [2636] on that exact quotation, and the note reads "Ps. liii. 1". The wrong number was inherited from the translator, in the series' Hebrew numbering, though the study is what printed it bare and in the wrong system. Because a reader checking the study against that edition would otherwise meet an unexplained disagreement, the References entry in sections/90-apparatus.tex now states the divergence as a fact about the edition: its note reads "Ps. liii. 1" while the words its own text prints are those of Ps 13:1 (Heb. 14:1), with the two psalms' Latin set side by side. Nothing in the reading's argument turns on it; the account of Chrysostom's alternating proofs is unchanged. Of the two standing advisories, STU-012 is cleared and STU-006 is not this stage's to clear. STU-012: the second reading's Postcommunion paragraph ended "The reading records the prayer and claims nothing from it", a sentence about what the guide had declined to infer rather than about the prayer; it is deleted, and the paragraph keeps its opening statement that the Postcommunion adds nothing distinctive to this reading together with the three grounds already given. A sweep for the same habit finds no other instance -- the three remaining uses of "declines" all have a Father (Cassiodorus twice, Jerome once) as their subject. STU-006 asks that research/interpretations.md section 3 record Aquinas among the just-judge-merciful-hearer reading's witnesses, in its 3.3 Offertory row and its 3.4 moral sense. The defect is real and the evidence sound -- research/scope.md 3.7 holds the locus, the Dessain 1857 vol. 2 p. 398 page image and the exact source role, and proper-components.toml and sections/40-just-judge-merciful-hearer.tex already agree -- but the file is not this stage's. workflows/fragments/proper-study/research.md gives research/interpretations.md to the research stage to write, the author-study fragment gives it to this stage only to read as the evidence map, and research/review-dependencies.toml records that the engine seals the leaf's research records. The edit was drafted, then reverted on finding that ownership, and the file is byte-identical to how this dispatch found it; research/production-review.md reports it for the cold reviewer to route upstream, as the iteration-2 and iteration-4 entries did. It needs the research owner, not another study pass. The settled proof is build/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/57-seventeenth-after-pentecost.pdf, SHA-256 4903f3c930fdf66e7ecf135b08b5731ec7165f1f815b0751807328787c847367, 38 physical pages (inside 20-50), revision timestamp 2026-09-19T05:00:00Z. It settles in two passes, and two independent builds from a removed PDF, log and auxiliary file produced identical bytes, so the proof is a cold fixed point; the log has no error, no LaTeX Warning, no package warning (the fancyhdr headheight warning a wrapped head would raise is absent), no overfull or underfull box, no undefined reference and no rerun request. The repair did not repaginate: the contents file and the auxiliary file are byte-identical to iteration 4's (4274428cbe0909d605fbb4b80de5f17d1ab066e01df1a6e0a85afb6b59ce3c3c and 424bc0ef72e2d0ac85f563b68d162d8215fd8194b71d44336471adebd423eeb9), so the page numbers the study review cites still name the passages it read, and the three touched passages stay where the findings placed them -- the Chrysostom paragraph on page 15, the Postcommunion paragraph on page 24, the References entry on page 37. Extent: 19,242 extracted words against the iteration-4 proof's 19,187 by the same plain pdftotext method, and a multiset diff of the two extractions accounts for every one of the 55 with nothing over -- 60 words added by the References note, 10 removed with the deleted sentence, 2 gained because the corrected citation turns one token into three, and 3 because misericordiam, Postcommunion and disagreements now break across lines; the rest is running heads, folios and table cells the layout extraction emits in a different order, netting to zero. Measured as substantive words instead -- the six argumentative components through Pandoc's LaTeX AST with headings and tables removed, the description the record's header gives -- this iteration's implementation counts 13,006 before and 12,998 now, a loss of 8, being the citation's +2 in the first reading and the deleted sentence's -10 in the second; the References note falls in the apparatus, which that measure excludes, which is why the two measures move opposite ways. As at iterations 2 and 4 the absolute figure does not reproduce the record's 13,106, so only the delta is comparable. All seventeen checks pass at these bytes: check-proper-components (artifacts/research), scripts/_proper_study.py check (content/research, --require-presentation), all twelve check-content-preflight checks the study gate names including provenance-matches-run against this packet's header, check-generation-metadata, check-web-edition, and a trial tools/web-edition conversion. house-voice passing is the mechanical half of the STU-012 repair, and the note added for STU-011 states facts about an edition, taking neither the guide nor its apparatus as its subject. All 38 pages were rendered and both contact sheets read, with pages 15, 24, 37 and 38 inspected individually: no blank page, no heading-only page, no clipping, collision or missing text, every running head a single line. Both companions were rebuilt against the changed shared generation-metadata.tex and build cleanly at their unchanged extents, 12 and 5 pages; they are the derivation stages' to rewrite. generation-metadata.tex carries the new shared timestamp and the iteration-5 contribution, and research/production-review.md records the repair, the corrected premise, the cleared advisory, the one reported upstream, the word counts and the proof. Files touched: sections/20-whole-heart-one-body.tex, sections/30-son-and-lord-of-david.tex, sections/90-apparatus.tex, generation-metadata.tex and research/production-review.md. No research evidence was changed and no claim was weakened to make anything pass. The shared-timestamp three-document build and the independent reviews remain the workflow's to obtain.
